Performers
Enrico Caruso (tenor), Salvatore Cottone (piano) Documented

Both the Commons description and the opened upstream transfer explicitly credit piano accompaniment. This is not an orchestral recording; no orchestral instrument is described in its listening notes.

[1] [2]
Work version
Piano-accompanied acoustic recording; exact reduction unestablished Documented

Tenor and piano are explicitly documented. No score for Cottone’s particular reduction has been identified; no orchestra timeline is supplied.

[1]
Recorded
1902-04-11 Documented

The original transfer description identifies 11 April 1902; Commons repeats it. The 2011 YouTube and 2018 Commons uploads are not recording dates.

[1] [2]
Place
Grand Hotel, Milan, Italy Documented

City/place as stated in the cited recording source; no more precise room or studio inferred.

[2]
Label
Gramophone & Typewriter / Gramophone Concert Record Inferred, not documented

Historical identification is inferred by combining the named 1902 performance in the transfer description with Friedman’s first-session matrix discussion and the reproduced G.C. 52349 label. The exact disc used by this transfer is not demonstrated.

[3] [4]
Catalogue
G.C. 52349 — historical issue associated with the 1902 recording; source pressing unestablished Inferred, not documented

Historical identification is inferred by combining the named 1902 performance in the transfer description with Friedman’s first-session matrix discussion and the reproduced G.C. 52349 label. The exact disc used by this transfer is not demonstrated.

[3] [4]
Matrix, take, sides
1790 — historical matrix associated with Caruso’s April 1902 recording; take and source-pressing markings unestablished Inferred, not documented

Historical identification is inferred by combining the named 1902 performance in the transfer description with Friedman’s first-session matrix discussion and the reproduced G.C. 52349 label. The exact disc used by this transfer is not demonstrated.

[3] [4]
Transfer
Tom Frøkjær — upstream uploader and presenter of the direct 78 transfer Documented

The video title calls this a direct transfer from an original 78 and the channel is Tom Frøkjær. A separate engineer credit is not supplied. No restoration method, transfer equipment or transfer date is inferred.

[2]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No transfer date established. The Commons, Archive and YouTube upload dates are not treated as digitisation or restoration dates.

[1]
Processing
Unknown Unknown

The source identifies a direct 78 transfer but does not document equalisation, denoising, pitch correction or speed correction.

[1] [2]
Composition rights
Underlying Puccini composition and historical libretto are public domain where ordinary life-plus-70 terms apply; no modern edition is claimed cleared. Documented

Commons marks the historical work public domain. This does not by itself establish the sound recording’s rights; the recording basis is separately documented below.

[1] [6]
Recording rights
Rule 2 — United States public domain: the original 1902 Caruso sound recording was commercially pressed before 1923. Documented

This is a sound-recording basis, not a grant inferred from the composer-only tag. Friedman documents early pressings of matrix 1790 and a metal-part marking in use during 1903–⁠1905; the source transfer identifies the April 1902 performance. Its particular pressing is unknown. The YouTube page supplies no separate CC licence and none is asserted. No worldwide clearance claim.

[1] [2] [3] [4] [7]

Giacomo Puccini, Tosca: E lucevan le stelle. Enrico Caruso, tenor; Salvatore Cottone, piano; Milan, 11 April 1902. Direct 78 transfer presented by Tom Frøkjær, YouTube kIMt7i7zeFc, imported by Racconish to Wikimedia Commons. Rights statement

  1. Wikimedia Commons — E lucevan le stelle (1902).opus — Description explicitly names Caruso and Cottone’s piano; 11 April 1902; source YouTube kIMt7i7zeFc; upload by Racconish in 2018 and Opus metadata; MP3 derivative. Upload and session kept distinct.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  2. Tom Frøkjær — Caruso, E lucevan le stelle, direct transfer from original 78 — Opened video description: first recording session, Grand Hotel in Milan, 11 April 1902; Salvatore Cottone piano. Channel Tom Frøkjær, upload 7 September 2011. No CC or non-commercial licence stated in the returned description. No musical audition claimed.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  3. Howard Friedman — Collector’s Guide to Gramophone Company Record Labels, page 7 — Discussion of multiple pressings of matrix 1790, Caruso’s first E lucevan from April 1902, and CO markings dating metal parts to 1903–⁠1905. Primary-label reproductions accompany the analysis.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  4. Gramophone Concert Record G.C. 52349 — reproduced label — Opened image: red Gramophone Concert Record label, G.C. 52349, Milan. Reproduction illustrates the historical issue, not the unidentified disc used for this transfer.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  5. Opéra national de Paris — Tosca, 2025–⁠26 — Acts I–III synopses; Roman locations, painter and Attavanti, Scarpia’s coercion, letter before execution. Used for dramatic context, not timings.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  6. Puccini Festival — Giacomo Puccini — Biography and work entries: early church work, Milan studies, librettists, source authors, premieres, composer’s death in 1924.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  7. U.S. Copyright Office — Classics Protection and Access Act — Term: recordings first published before 1923 ceased receiving the specified federal remedies after 31 December 2021. Sound-recording basis, distinct from composition copyright.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
